sources_and_data.source: Reidl-Wahlström, Parameterized Algorithms for Zero Extension and Metric Labelling Problems
sources_and_data.use: source definition, exact k-bounded metric-sparsifier target, fixed-s O(k^(s+1)) baseline
local source/novelty audit and mismatch boundaries for later flow, cut, and retracted claims

method.type: direct mathematical proof and adversarial source audit; no experiment
method.construction: delete terminal-free leaves and suppress nonterminal degree-two paths
method.boundary_signature: for each suppressed path, sigma_P(a,b)=(mu(a,b), 1[a != b]); graph schema is independent of D, mu, tau, and k
method.quantifiers: all finite metrics on at most s labels, all injective terminal labelings, and all integers k >= 0
two_sided_maps: tree to core: triangle inequality lowers cost and endpoint disagreement lowers crossings
core to tree: label every suppressed path internally by one endpoint, preserving both cost and crossings

source_definition_restatement.objective: minimum sum of metric distances over edges among extensions of an injective terminal labeling
source_definition_restatement.preservation: exact equality of restricted optima for every admissible metric and terminal labeling
source_definition_restatement.threshold_note: source notation includes q, but q is not needed for this exact equality lemma

mathematical_claim: For every finite connected unweighted tree T with terminal set S, its terminal core C preserves OPT_{T,k}(mu,tau) exactly for every admissible metric, injective terminal labeling, and k. For m=|S|>=2, |E(C)|<=2m-3.
assumptions: T is a finite connected unweighted tree and S is its designated terminal set.
D is finite, mu is a metric on D, and tau:S->D is injective; |D|<=s is only a parameter bound.
The restricted objective counts every tree edge with unit multiplicity and imposes only the upper bound cr(lambda)<=k.
The sparsifier is allowed to retain all terminals and replace terminal-free leaves and nonterminal degree-two paths by the stated terminal core.
verified_steps: Deleting a terminal-free leaf and copying its parent's label preserves both optimum cost and crossing feasibility in both directions.
For every suppressed path, triangle inequality maps any tree labeling to an endpoint edge of no greater cost, while endpoint disagreement is no more than the path's crossing count.
A core labeling extends by making every suppressed path constant except at one endpoint, giving exactly the endpoint metric cost and disagreement bit; deleted leaves copy their parent.
All core leaves are terminals and all nonterminals have degree at least three, so the tree degree identity yields |E(C)|<=2|S|-3 for |S|>=2.
The construction and both inequalities contain no s-dependent exponent; only the explicit terminal factor O(|S|)<=O(s) remains.

excluded_claims: No conclusion for weighted trees, cacti, or general graphs.
No conclusion about a universal sparsifier exponent for unrestricted graphs.
No asymptotic lower bound is inferred.
